correctness.rationale: The RESULT.md vertex normalization gives a genuine edge-2 regular icosahedron. A fresh independent exact SymPy implementation computes every det(v_j-v_i,v_k-v_i,v_l-v_i) for all C(12,4)=495 quadruples and classifies exact magnitudes as 0,4,4φ,4φ²,4φ³ with frequencies 75,30,180,180,30. There are exactly 30 maximal vertex supports. Independent support counting over all C(12,3)=220 triples yields multiplicity counts 140 bases with 0 allowed apices, 60 with 1, 20 with 3; the 20 triple-apex sets are precisely the 20 supporting icosahedron faces, and all corresponding oriented determinants agree. Every 30 extreme 4-vertex sets belongs to two base–facet families. A separate exact maximum-hypergraph check excludes any complete 2x2 grid of maximal supports over any fixed vertex pair, precluding two or more simultaneously movable vertices in the positive convex expansions; coincident support indices would give determinant zero and are also excluded. Determinant multiaffinity implies that absolute maximality for arbitrary four points in the convex polytope forces every positive-weight vertex quadruple to share the same maximal oriented determinant. Therefore any extremal tetrahedron has three actual icosahedral vertices and the remaining point in the corresponding opposite triangular facet. All such points attain the same determinant by affine dependence. The icosahedron volume equals 20φ²/3 by 20 face pyramids, giving sharp tetrahedron volume (4φ³)/6=2φ³/3 and ratio φ/10. This proves the full continuous classification, not merely a sampled finite bound.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge originality passes. The exact 495-subset volume multiset, maximum icosahedral volume fraction, and complete 20-facet two-dimensional continuum of maximizers were not implied by inspected published theorems. Horváth–Lángi optimize polytopes with freely chosen points on the circumsphere, with a regular tetrahedron as the sphere-wide optimum, not a tetrahedron confined to the icosahedron. Horváth (2014) bounds volumes of entire 12-vertex icosahedra and facial tetrahedra with center apex, not an arbitrary maximum tetrahedron inside a fixed icosahedron. Conway–Torquato (2006) pack 20 constrained regular center-apex tetrahedra and do not give the unrestricted four-vertex determinant spectrum. Searches also considered published related exact regular-24-cell/simplex findings; their different dimensions and host objects give no domination. Absolute historical priority is not certified.
residual_risks: Historical priority in Coxeter-era regular-polytope sources, recreational geometry, theses or specialized icosahedral enumerations is not fully settled.
The full Conway–Torquato article was inaccessible through the opened OA page; assessed only material actually indexed and read; targeted relevant Appendix evidence is available.
Neither unsuccessful semantic searches nor independent enumeration alone certify absolute novelty.

value.rationale: The maximal volume of a simplex contained in a familiar regular convex body is a natural and geometrically meaningful invariant. The entire four-vertex tetrahedral volume spectrum with multiplicities is a complete canonical finite classification rather than an arbitrary case slice. The surprising uncountable 20-facet non-rigid equality locus, including the distinction between only 30 vertex-supported optimizers and continuously movable opposite-facet apexes, is needed to understand equality in the convex maximization problem. These precise facts could be reused in regular-polytope geometry and constrained simplex-volume problems even without a broader theorem or large downstream application. Its significance is mathematical completeness and equality structure, not simply having a reproducible computation.
residual_risks: If an older comprehensive icosahedron volume/equality table exists, the novelty component and thus original scientific value would require reconsideration.
The work does not generalize the locus to arbitrary host polytopes, though no such generalization is necessary for the assessed natural exact invariant.
